concerns.text: The spec restricts the sensitivity analysis to varying the propensity score caliper (0.01, 0.05, 0.1). The idea explicitly lists 'difference-in-differences' as an alternative causal identification strategy in the 'Methodology sketch' and 'How this project addresses the gap' sections. The spec drops this alternative entirely, focusing solely on PSM. If PSM fails balance or common support, the spec has no fallback mechanism defined other than halting, whereas the idea suggested a broader methodological toolkit.

The idea specifies outcome variables including 'Socioeconomic Proxy (e.g., home value appreciation or credit score changes if available in linked datasets)'. The spec's User Story 1 and FR-002 only define 'energy cost burden' and 'disposable income'. The socioeconomic proxy outcome is missing from the spec's data ingestion and variable construction requirements, despite being a core part of the research question's 'socioeconomic outcomes' triad.
